## Purpose

`integration_schedule_due` coalesces periodic or manual triggers into the
project's durable request. The root runtime seeds a Subject for that request;
the Subject's pinned policy decides when to seal and publish. There is no
`integration.sweep_due` event cascade or manual flush control.

## How it works internally

The handler validates the project and caller scope, then delegates to
[`IntegrationScheduler.mark_due`](../../../src/integration/scheduler.py).
Under the project lock, the scheduler checks train mode, draining state and
the configured interval. It advances elapsed windows once, retains the exact
outstanding request, and records one catch-up when work is already active.
New requests receive a monotone project sequence. Restart recovery uses those
durable identities instead of a second event scheduler.

## Side effects and results

The command updates the existing project schedule and may maintain its active
batch lease. It performs no Git writes, creates no task and enqueues no sweep
event. `due` means a durable request was recorded; `not_due` means the interval
has not elapsed; `coalesced` retains an outstanding request and catch-up.
`disabled` refuses scheduling outside enabled train mode or during draining.
A caller outside the project receives `unauthorized`.

Read the schedule and Subject evidence with `aq integration status PROJECT_ID`.
For delivery waits, see
[troubleshooting](../../guides/integration-troubleshooting.md#a-passed-task-blocked-at-delivery).
